extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of CCR management units (CCRMU), facility permit authorities, state and federal environmental regulators, and permitting reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements, performance standards, documentation, and permitting/deferral procedures for closing Coal Combustion Residuals Management Units (CCRMU), including units beneath critical infrastructure and previously closed units. Covers which performance standards apply, timelines/deadlines, and what permit authorities must evaluate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to meet §257.102 performance standards for CCRMU closures
rubrics_metrics.description: This final rule requires that the closure of CCRMU meet the performance standards in either §257.102(c) or (d). Under this final rule all closures initiated after the effective date of this rule, as well as those that were not completed prior to the effective date of this rule, will need to comply with these requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closures that meet §257.102(c) or §257.102(d) are considered compliant; closures initiated after effective date must comply. EPA notes RCRA requires setting minimum criteria to prevent harm (citing USWAG).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation (not automatic re-closure) of previously closed CCRMU
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is not requiring previously closed CCRMU to automatically re-close but simply to evaluate whether the unit meets the requirements of §257.102(d), and if they do not, to take such measures as are necessary to bring the unit into compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prior closure can be certified to meet the applicable §257.102 standard, the unit need only post documentation. If not, site-specific remedial or engineering measures may be required rather than a full "re-closure."

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral conditions for CCRMU located beneath critical infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is deferring the requirement to initiate closure of CCRMU located beneath critical infrastructure until either: (1) The infrastructure is no longer essential for the activity to be successful; (2) A permit authority determines closure is necessary to ensure there will be no reasonable probability of adverse effect on health or the environment; or (3) The closure or decommissioning of the facility, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferral is intended to allow case-by-case permitting decisions to balance environmental risks against reliability and operational risks associated with disturbing critical infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional condition for deferral under active disposal units (location or dewatering standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for the deferral, the facility must document that the CCRMU meets one of two existing performance standards: either (1) The standard in §257.60 that the unit was constructed with a base located no less than 1.52 m (5 feet) above the upper limit of the uppermost aquifer, or must demonstrate there is no intermittent, recurring, or sustained hydraulic connection between any portion of the CCR unit and the upper limit of the uppermost aquifer or surface water; or (2) The dewatering standard in §257.102(d)(2)(i) that all free liquids have been eliminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA expects the §257.60 location standard to be directly applicable to many CCRMU landfills; dewatering standard applies to closed CCR surface impoundments. This condition addresses why many previous closures did not meet RCRA section 4004(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation requirements in FER Part 2 (§257.75(d)) for deferral eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner/operator of a CCRMU located under critical infrastructure must include information documenting their eligibility for the deferral in the FER part 2 in §257.75(d) that includes at a minimum a description of the infrastructure, its current and anticipated use(s), and the decommissioning date or anticipated active lifespan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The documentation must also demonstrate compliance with either §257.60 or §257.102(d)(2)(i), and that the structures are both (1) necessary for continued generation or ongoing site activity and (2) not readily replaced or relocated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the permit application process to evaluate deferral and closure necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: When the permit application is called in, the facility must provide sufficient information, including data on contaminant levels in groundwater, to demonstrate that the criteria for the deferral have been met, and for the permit authority to be able to evaluate the risks associated with the CCRMU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA intends to rely on permitting as the primary mechanism to collect groundwater, soil, and analytical data needed to determine whether closure is necessary to mitigate unacceptable risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines: initiation and completion timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA has extended the deadline to initiate closure to Tuesday, May 8, 2029, which is 54 months after the effective date of this final rule. Depending on the CCRMU, the facility may have as much as an additional seven to 15 years to complete closure; for many landfills a seven-year deadline is more likely applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA extended deadlines in part because some performance standards (e.g., §257.102(d)(2)) can take significant time to meet. Facilities should plan for the extended initiation timeline and variable completion periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-closure care and limited applicability where prior closure meets §257.102
rubrics_metrics.description: If a facility can certify that prior closure of a unit meets the performance standards in §257.102(c) it only needs to post documentation. If a facility can demonstrate that the closed unit meets the requirements under §257.102(d), EPA will consider the unit to be closed and the only requirements applicable are those for closed units under post-closure care (groundwater monitoring and, if necessary, corrective action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA never intended to require facilities that otherwise met the closure standards to re-close the unit; documentation and certification suffice where standards are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for deferral of prior State-law or CERCLA/RCRA Subtitle C closures to permitting
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is deferring the requirement for a CCRMU that closed prior to the effective date of this rule to demonstrate compliance with §257.102(d) until a permit application if the facility can document that: a regulatory authority actively oversaw and approved the closure; the regulatory action was via a permit, administrative order, or consent order issued after 2015 or under an EPA-approved RCRA State program; and groundwater monitoring was required to ensure no contamination not addressed by corrective action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferral is limited to closures where a regulatory authority played an active role and the permit/order required ongoing groundwater monitoring until cleanup standards were achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance standards for groundwater monitoring systems (subset of §257.91(a)) for demonstrating equivalency
rubrics_metrics.description: To support deferral of a prior closure as substantially equivalent, the facility must demonstrate that the groundwater monitoring system was capable of: (1) Accurately representing background water quality, (2) Accurately representing the quality of water passing the waste boundary, and (3) Detecting contamination in the uppermost aquifer. The groundwater monitoring system must have monitored all potential contaminant pathways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA requires specifics of monitoring design and results to evaluate whether prior closures are protective; generalized or vague statements are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for a site-specific risk assessment and regulatory oversight for equivalency
rubrics_metrics.description: A facility would need to demonstrate that a site-specific risk assessment was conducted or approved by the regulatory authority prior to (or as part of) approving the closure, and that the closure and any necessary corrective action has been overseen by the regulatory authority, pursuant to an enforceable requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The risk assessment and regulatory oversight must be documented and available to support deferral to permitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation, applicability report, operating record, and certification for deferral/equivalency
rubrics_metrics.description: The facility must prepare and include documentation in the applicability report and operating record demonstrating it met the criteria and is eligible for deferral. The documentation must include specifics including the State permit, order, data, groundwater monitoring results, etc., and must be certified by the owner/operator or an authorized representative using the same language in §257.102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the permit application is called in, EPA or an approved State Director will review these materials to determine equivalency; lack of necessary specifics will prevent a deferral determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit authority determinations and outcomes for equivalency
rubrics_metrics.description: If EPA or an approved State Director determines that the closure has met the appropriate part 257 closure standard, EPA or an approved State Director will issue a post-closure permit. If determined not to meet part 257 standards, the owner/operator will be required to submit a permit application for an operating permit and EPA will issue a permit containing the specific requirements necessary to achieve compliance with §257.102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The permitting process is the vehicle to require additional measures or full closure if the prior closure is not equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expansion of §257.102(d)(2) drainage and stabilization standards to all CCR units with liquids
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is revising §257.102(d)(2) so that it applies to all CCR units and CCRMU where free liquids remain in the unit. The existing (d)(2) performance standards for drainage and stabilization (including (d)(2)(i) and (ii)) are critical to ensuring units that contain liquids are properly and safely closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These standards must be met prior to installing the final cover system required under paragraph (d)(3). If there are no liquids in the unit, the revision does not require action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and regulatory scope of "contains CCR and liquids" and related definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA finalized the requirement to apply the (d)(2) performance standards rather than adopt the commenter-proposed alternate text, noting concern the suggested revision would be redundant of the new definition of "contains CCR and liquids" and not clearly communicate regulated entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA is finalizing as proposed and will enforce applicability based on its definitions; commenters' alternative text was rejected for potential ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engineering measures and remedial options for closures with groundwater contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Where unlined waste units are continually or periodically in contact with groundwater, more extensive closure techniques such as engineering controls designed to prevent groundwater from flowing through waste or to stabilize the waste and fix contaminants in place may be attempted, or excavation and clean closure of the unit may ultimately be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA lists examples of engineering measures that may be effective and should be considered, e.g., installation of slurry walls, interception trenches, or groundwater extraction wells to prevent groundwater infiltration. Effectiveness is site-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between closure standards (preventive) and corrective action (remedial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Closure-in-place standards are designed to ensure the waste in the closed unit has been dried out and is kept dry so that leachate cannot form and be released. By contrast, corrective action provisions contain standards and procedures for cleaning up contamination that has already leaked out of the unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA emphasizes that closure and corrective action are distinct and independent requirements; reliance solely on corrective action rather than closure is insufficient to meet part 257 objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "critical infrastructure" for deferral purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is defining 'critical infrastructure' as infrastructure, large buildings, or other structures vital to the success or continuation of current site operations or activities for the public welfare. This does not include infrastructure, large buildings, or other structures that solely provide commercial or financial benefit to private entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structures must be both (1) necessary for continued generation or current site activity, and (2) not readily replaced or relocated. Examples: high power electric transmission towers, large buildings, electrical substations; a replaceable parking lot would not qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of electric grid reliability and coordination with balancing authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA recognizes closure of CCRMU beneath critical energy production infrastructure may adversely affect grid reliability (e.g., voltage support, local resource adequacy) and that actions requiring taking generating units offline may be constrained by regional transmission organizations (RTOs) and other reliability authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of these reliability concerns EPA is deferring mandatory closure deadlines for such CCRMU to permitting to allow consultation and case-by-case consideration; facilities should follow mandated outage procedures from balancing authorities and state entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that groundwater monitoring and corrective action continue where applicable even during deferral
rubrics_metrics.description: These units will be required to comply with all other requirements applicable to CCRMU, including the requirements for groundwater monitoring and corrective action, if necessary, even when closure initiation is deferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferral of initiation to permitting does not exempt a unit from ongoing monitoring and corrective action obligations under part 257.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standard for State-claimed equivalency examples
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA requires sufficient detail to evaluate the adequacy of State closures; generalized claims (e.g., 'monitoring in place' without details) do not demonstrate equivalency to part 257 standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples must include specifics on groundwater monitoring required, scope, data demonstrating lack of impact, permits/orders, and monitoring results; absence of such specifics prevents EPA from finding a broad exemption.
